newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Horse Racing-Danoli in good form ahead of Naas.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-Danoli in good form ahead of Naas.

text.p: Trainer Tom Foley said on Friday that his stable-star Danoli had worked well in training at home this morning and was in good form ahead of Saturday's Novice Chase at Naas. "He worked well this morning and is in good form. He is eating well and has come out of the Clonmel race well," the Bagenalstown-based handler said.
Ireland's equine hero will face nine opponents in the two-mile race, due to start at 1430 GMT, which is sure to be the feature event on the seven race card.
Danoli enjoyed a winning start to his chasing career at Clonmel racecourse, southern Ireland, on November 1.
"He took to jumping fences very, very well," Philip Fenton, who deputised for the injured Tommy Treacy on the occasion said.
Danoli caught the imagination of the Irish racing public in 1994 when he landed the Cheltenham Sun Alliance Novice Hurdle before he went on to win the Aintree Hurdle in Liverpool.
The following year Danoli finished third behind Alderbrook and Large Action respectively in the Cheltenham Champion Hurdle.
Danoli broke a fetlock bone during the running of the 1995 Aintree Hurdle but on that occasion he overcame the pain barrier to retain his title in style.
He returned to top class action last season when he finished fourth in the Cheltenham Champion Hurdle and third in the Aintree Hurdle.
Danoli was bought by Foley on behalf of owner Dan O'Neill for 7,000 Irish pounds.
